context: R28 repeated public-node TCP-reachable but HTTP-path-invalid failures

claims.claim: Installed pool had 475 public nodes; 336 were quick-test eligible in the latest live gate, while repeated full-path samples returned PATH_NOT_VERIFIED_NODE and honest N/A throughput.
Trojan share links can omit a security=tls parameter because TLS is intrinsic/default in Trojan/Trojan-Go semantics; the prior parser enabled TLS only when security=tls/reality was explicit.
sing-box WebSocket transport supports max_early_data and early_data_header_name; Xray WebSocket uses ed to enable early data and Sec-WebSocket-Protocol compatibility.
sing-box 1.14 transport model supports HTTP, WebSocket, QUIC, gRPC and HTTPUpgrade; it does not support XHTTP/mKCP in this transport interface, so unsupported transports remain fail-closed.
Keep cheap endpoint reachability separate from full HTTP-path verification; failed throughput is N/A rather than 0 Mbps; do not weaken path verification.
Benchmark remains bounded to four candidates per wave but prioritizes under-tested protocols before source diversity, preventing VMess/SS/Hysteria2 starvation behind large VLESS/Trojan pools.

limitations: Public free nodes are untrusted and volatile; TCP reachability does not prove proxy validity.
A successful parser mapping does not prove a public credential/server is still alive.
Trusted Windows code signing remains an external gate.
